title: Handley Page Halifax JP137
memorial_details: Stone of remembrance with a triangular pediment set on a marble base with two miliary badges centrally and the lettering in white.
inscription:
MOORDOWN
HALIFAX MEMORIAL
IN MEMORY OF THE TWO LOCAL RESIDENTS
AND SEVEN AIRCREW WHO LOST THEIR LIVES
IN THE CAUSE OF FREEDOM
WHEN RAF HALIFAX BOMBER JP 137 CRASHED
AT THIS LOCATION ON 21st MARCH 1944
Mrs. DOROTHEA BENNETT Flat 9 Meadow Court
Mr. PERCY F. CHISLETT 1027 Wimborne Road
Sgt. DENIS R. EVANS Pilot RAFVR
Sgt. HENRY W. ROBERTS Nav. RAFVR
F/O STANLEY A. APPLETON B/A RAFVR
Sgt. GEORGE A. ALEXANDER W/Op. RAFVR
Sgt. STANLEY F. GENT F/E RAFVR
Sgt. KENNETH GREEN A/G RAFVR
Sgt. REGINALD R. McGREGOR A/G RCAF
'LEST WE FORGET'
ORGANISED BY THE MOORDOWN 2010 COMMITTEE
AS A CONTRIBUTION TO THE BICENTENARY OF BOURNEMOUTH

sources.title: International Bomber Command Centre losses database (Sgt D R Evans)
The Moordown Halifax Memorial (Moordown Local History Society)

narrative:
In the early hours of 21 March 1944, Halifax II JP137 took off from RAF Hurn at 00:33 on a transfer flight to Morocco. Within moments the aircraft developed engine trouble. It turned in a wide arc, apparently trying to get back to Hurn, but came down in Moordown. It clipped buildings along Wimborne Road, including a Victorian chapel and the tram depot, and crashed at the corner of Wimborne Road and Meadow Court Close with full fuel tanks.

All seven crew were killed, the youngest aged 20. So were two people on the ground: Mrs Dorothea Bennett of Flat 9 Meadow Court and Mr Percy Chislett of 1027 Wimborne Road. The official report blamed the 20-year-old pilot, Sgt Denis Evans, although eyewitnesses saw an engine on fire just before impact.

The memorial was proposed during Bournemouth's bicentenary in 2010. It was organised by the Moordown 2010 Committee and unveiled and dedicated on 10 July 2011, on the spot where the aircraft came down. The 70th and 80th anniversaries have both been marked at the memorial.

community_connection: Organised by the Moordown 2010 Committee for Bournemouth's bicentenary and unveiled in July 2011. The Moordown Local History Society keeps the memorial's story at jp137.com, and anniversaries are still marked at the stone.
crew_summary: 7 crew, all killed, and 2 Moordown residents killed on the ground
cause_of_loss: Engine failure shortly after take-off from RAF Hurn; eyewitnesses reported an engine on fire before impact

maintainer.organisation: Moordown 2010 Committee (memorial organisers); Moordown Local History Society (jp137.com)
maintainer.notes: The memorial was organised by the Moordown 2010 Committee. The Moordown Local History Society runs jp137.com, the memorial's website, and can be contacted through its feedback form. Moordown is unparished; the local authority is BCP Council (Moordown ward).

local_contacts.role: Local authority (Moordown has no parish council)
